Operator: Good day, and welcome to the GlobalCom Inc. Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by the number of the line you'd like to ask the question from. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalCom Inc.'s Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in Q2, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment across our telecom and media operations. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth through our converged wireless, fiber, and digital content strategy.

Our achievements include robust revenue growth from premium 5G services and fiber expansions, alongside steady media streaming momentum. We are also seeing substantial growth from our GlobalStream+ platform with a significant uptick in bundled subscribers. Further, we are concentrating on enterprise solutions leveraging private 5G networks. Additionally, network reliability enhancements are showing promise. We are also improving customer retention through personalized bundles. We are strategically investing in edge computing and AI-driven efficiencies. Finally, sustainability initiatives are underway and we are exploring partnerships for next-gen content delivery.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $28.7 billion, representing a 4.2% year-over-year increase and 2.1% quarter-over-quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 billion, resulting in a margin of 39%, up 420 basis points year-over-year. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $4.2 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

Good afternoon, everyone—let me dive deeper into our revenue mix analysis, specifically the contribution by segment with a percentage breakdown. This quarter's consolidated revenues reflect disciplined execution across our core pillars in this dynamic telecom and media landscape. Our four primary reporting segments represent 98% of total revenues, with the rest from device sales and equipment leasing.

Mobile Services accounted for 55% of total revenue at $15.8 billion, up 5.8% year-over-year. This is our largest and most resilient segment, up from 53% a year ago as we capture share in the postpaid wireless market. Postpaid ARPU rose 3.1% to $58.42, driven by our 5G Standalone rollout covering 85% of our 120 million North American subscriber base and 65% in Europe. We saw a 7.2% increase in 5G subscriber adds to 62 million total, with premium Unlimited Plus plans—offering mmWave speeds up to 4 Gbps and early access to 5G Advanced—driving 42% of net adds. Fixed wireless access contributed $1.2 billion or 8% of segment revenue, especially in suburban U.S. markets competing with T-Mobile's FWA and Starlink. North America drove 72% of growth, Europe 12% via spectrum auctions and MVNO partnerships like Vodafone UK. We're monetizing 5G through enterprise slicing for AR/VR and autonomous vehicles, targeting $2 billion run-rate by FY2025.

Fixed Broadband and Wireline made up 22% at $6.3 billion, up 6.4% year-over-year, our fastest-growing area amid the fiber arms race. Revenues grew with 12% more FTTH subscribers to 18 million, gigabit speeds standard, pushing broadband ARPU to $72.50, up 4.7%. Our Fiber First initiative, with $4.2 billion capex this half, passed 25 million U.S. Sunbelt homes and expanded into European urban areas like Paris and Madrid. Hybrid bundles—68% of new adds pairing 1 Gbps+ fiber with mobile—reduced churn to under 1% monthly. U.S. contributed 65% of growth with $1.8 billion BEAD grants; Asia-Pacific pilots in Singapore test XGS-PON for 10 Gbps, eyeing 5% contribution by FY2026. Fiber's EBITDA margins expanded 250 basis points to 42% as we phase out copper DSL to 15%.

Media and Entertainment held at 15% with $4.3 billion, up 1.9%. Linear video stabilized at 28 million subs after a 2% decline, better than industry 5-7%. Streaming surged 18% to $2.1 billion via GlobalStream+ at 45 million paid subs, competing with Netflix and Disney+ through UFC exclusives and HBO co-productions. Ad-supported tiers drove 25% growth, FAST channels $450 million incremental ads. AI personalization boosted engagement 22% and ARPU $1.20. North America 55%, Europe 30% via Sky Italia, Brazil 10% mobile-first. Super Bundles—fiber + mobile + streaming for $120/month—lifted attachment to 62%.

Enterprise and Business Solutions rounded out at 6% with $1.7 billion, up 8.2%, high-margin at 52% EBITDA. Growth from 14% higher Fortune 1000 sales, SDx for cloud on-ramps like Verizon-AWS. Key win: $500 million deal for private 5G at 50+ warehouses for IoT/robotics. U.S. 60%, Europe 25% Deutsche Telekom synergies, Japan APAC growth. Targeting 10% total revenue by FY2027 via MEC.

Overall, the mix shift—mobile mid-50s, broadband up 200 bps, enterprise accelerating—shows our wireless + fiber + digital transition, services 92% of revenues up from 89%, equipment 3%. Blended margins up 110 bps to 38% via premiumization and opex discipline amid 3.8% inflation. Q3 outlook: $29.0-$29.5 billion, FWA $1.5 billion quarterly, fiber 30 million passes.

Now, on EBITDA margins, which hit 39.2%, up 420 basis points year-over-year from 35% and 110 sequentially. This is our strongest in five years, on track for 38.5% full-year, ahead of 36-37% guidance. Revenue grew 7.2% to $14.8 billion, outpacing opex 1.8%. Postpaid ARPU up 4.1% to $52.30 on 5G Unlimited and financing; broadband 6.5% subs to 28 million, FTTH 65% U.S. addresses; media up 12% on ad-tier and bundling.

Cost mitigation via supply chain, modernization, SG&A leverage—opex 52.4% of revenue, down 250 bps. Network opex 28%, $450 million savings from Open RAN at 25% U.S. RAN with Nokia/Rakuten, capex to 15.2%, energy 22% better via AI. Spectrum refarm post $2.1 billion C-band to 85% top MSAs, wireless margins 45.3% from 41.2%.

Wireless 55% revenues drove 60% expansion, margins 380 bps to 45.3%, churn 0.89% via 5G guarantee and Paramount+ perks. Broadband 42.8% up 510 bps on RGON and 15% CAC cut. Media 18% revenues to 22% margin on 45 million subs and Warner deals, linear fees down 8%.

North America 82% EBITDA, 450 bps to 41.1% on 5G SA, fiber overbuilds, 140 MHz midband advantage for 28% traffic. Europe 300 bps to 32.5% via dark fiber. APAC 35.2% steady, mmWave trials 10% capex save.

Five-year compound 250 bps from 30.8%, third straight sequential gain. Levers: AI ops 40% fault automation, 18% truck rolls down; 12% procurement; $2.5 billion FCF. Dividend up 8% to $0.85, 45-50% FCF payout, 60% FCF to broadband M&A. Target 42-45% by 2026 on 5G-Advanced, edge, NFL rights. Converged Edge strategy ahead of pure-plays.

Turning to debt levels and leverage. Gross debt $46.2 billion: $12.5 billion secured loans/revolvers, $28.7 billion IG notes, $5 billion CP. Cash $8.1 billion, net debt $38.1 billion. LTM EBITDA $13.4 billion up 8%, gross leverage 3.4x, net 2.8x—down from 4.0x/3.3x YoY, 3.7x YE23. Peer-low vs. Verizon 2.9x, Comcast 2.6x. Cost 4.1% down 40 bps on $3.5 billion refinance to 2033/2031 notes.

Organic EBITDA: wireless ARPU 4.2% to $58.50 on 5G SA 45% base, media bundles $2.50; media 250 bps to 22% on consolidations, 12% ads; FWA 450k subs $180 million EBITDA. Debt management: $1.2 billion buybacks, $2 billion repurchase delever 0.1x. Revolver undrawn $4.5 billion.

North America 75% EBITDA covers 120% capex, $800 million paydowns. Europe 15% spectrum refarm €1.2 billion payback <4 years, 15% data growth. APAC/LATAM 10% fiber 28% margins offset FX.

Tower sales 4,500 sites $2.8 billion, 0.2x delever annual; edge 30% colocation $500 million capex cut; spectrum leasebacks $400 million. Target mid-2x net by 2025, capex peak 14% to 12%, $6.2 billion FCF 85% conversion. Funds $4-5 billion dividends/buybacks, bolt-ons at 6-7x. Coverage 5.2x.

On net subscriber additions, overall 175,000 across residential and business, up 12% year-over-year, strongest since Q1 2022, ahead of industry 8%.

Residential +142,000 up 15%: broadband +98,000 on 1.2 million homes passed with 2Gig fiber, 28% penetration via Fiber First, Xbox bundles, Netflix/Disney+. Churn 0.85%. Wireless +44,000 postpaid on C-band 85% top markets, Unlimited Max. Video -2,000 offset by VeriStream +150,000. Northeast/Sun Belt 40%, Midwest BEAD 15,000. Sequential +8%.

Business +33,000 up 3%: SMB broadband/voice +18,000 on SD-WAN Cisco Meraki, healthcare/retail 99.999% SLAs. Enterprise +15,000 private 5G logistics, edge VeriCloud 11% ACV to $45,000. Churn 0.6%. Europe Vodafone +5,000 FWA, LATAM Mexico 2,000.

Converged Growth: 40 million fiber-eligible, 20% penetration 2025, churn down 15 bps AI Amdocs. Share gains on 2Gig+ 1.5 million +25%. Q4 guide 160-190k, residential high-end holiday bundles.

Content and Media generated $2.8 billion, 18% year-over-year up, 28% total revenue from 24%. Sequential 5%. SVOD/bundles $1.4 billion +22% on VoxTel Stream+ Disney/Netflix compete, 60% FWA/fiber bundles $75/month. AVOD/FAST $650 million +35%, 15 million MAUs OpenPath DSP Trade Desk/Google, FAST $150 million Warner. Linear $750 million flat, licensing EchoNet Sky/Canal+.

EBITDA $950 million, 34% margin up 300 bps YoY/150 sequential. Content amort $1.1 billion 39% revenue down from 42%, NBA/NFL. FCF $600 million 70% dividend. DVS 52 million +2.8 million QoQ +12% YoY: SVOD +1.9 million bundles 65%, AVOD/FAST MAUs 18.5 million +25% 40% broadband pen, churn 1.8% -14% AI WatchGuard +28% engagement, blended ARPU $14.25 +5%, SVOD $15.80 +6% $19.99 premium.

North America $2.1 billion +20% sports Thursday Football 500k cross-promo. Europe $420 million +12% Vodafone 450k DMA ads. APAC/LATAM $280 million +25% Jio/Brazil Claro ARPU $8.50 +10%.

Expansion: $4.5 billion content 40% originals EchoNet Fremantle, MLS WWE. HyperStream 5G <2s latency -15% churn. Shoppable Walmart $500 million FY25 +10% CPMs. M&A Paramount FAST 100 million MAUs. Q3 $2.9-3.0 billion 33-35% margins, FY DVS 58 million ARPU +7%.

Operating expense management yielded $285 million year-over-year savings, margins to 42.3% from 38.7%, 360 bps, $1.2 billion EBITDA add, FCF up 22%.

Network 45% OpEx $140 million save AI RIC Ericsson-like, energy -22% 150k sites, Europe 15% inflation. US Open RAN Nokia/Samsung interconnect -18% $45 million 30% edge. APAC $32 million FTTH India 15% lower. $200 million more 2024 5G SA 60%.

Content $420 million 12% below, $65 million renegotiate prune 25% ad-tiers Warner Max-like linear $40 million NFL alt, sunset 15 channels $25 million ARPU $28. Europe Sky FAST $18 million ratio 32% from 36%.

SG&A $80 million: AI Google Vertex 70% Tier1 -28% $35 million Verizon-like 50 million subs. Attrition/offshore 4,200 FTE $25 million. Marketing digital CTV Roku/Fire 40% 4.1x ROI from 2.8x.

Total OpEx $4.7 billion -8.2%, $2.8 billion EBITDA +15%. FCF $1.5 billion delever 2.6x. Target 44-46% 2025 Open RAN AI. US fiber <1200/pass 20% below, Europe Gigabit Directive APAC data.

Zero-based budgeting KPIs, Q3 <3% growth $11.2-11.5 billion EBITDA.

Cost of revenue $11.4 billion +4.2% YoY 48% revenue from 47%. 3.8% CAGR past three years vs revenue 2.9%, steady mid-40s, cost/sub $28.50 -2.1% AI SDN.

Network/interconnect $5.8 billion +7.4% 51%: data 15.5 EB +22% 5G SA 45 million +35%, FWA; peering OTT Netflix/YouTube paid Comcast-like +9%. Open RAN -8%, edge -15% retransmits.

Content $2.3 billion +4.5% 20%: linear 28 million -5% streaming ARPU $15.20 +12% TeleStream+ NBA/Premier +6%, Edgeworld amort. Windowing 45 days multi-license $120 million save FAST 18% offset.

Provisioning $1.7 billion +3% 15%: 1.2 million broadband fiber $450/install from $520 self-kits 40% drone. Enterprise 5G auto $50 million.

D&A $1.4 billion -6.7% 12%: 4G sunset 30% sites, VNF NFV longer lives 400Gbps 85%.

North America 75% +5% C-band California. Europe 15% +2% Vodafone Spain roaming caps. APAC/LATAM 10% +8% 4G refarm -12%/GB.

AI/ML predictive 1.2 million sites -11% $650 million, Open RAN 15 markets 25% capex Qualcomm/Samsung. AWS Akamai -20% transit blockchain rights. Q3 $11.6-11.8 billion 2-3% +200 bps FY25.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage to 85% of key markets and increasing capacity for 22% data growth. We're investing in network slicing and edge computing to enable low-latency apps like AR/VR and IoT. Uptime remains at 99.999%, and we're improving spectral efficiency through Open RAN deployments now at 25% of our RAN.

David Kim: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth with 175,000 net adds and improved satisfaction scores to record highs. Bundled offerings like fiber-mobile-streaming at $120/month resonate, attachment at 62%. We're focused on increasing enterprise penetration through private 5G wins, targeting 10% revenue share.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are driving innovation with AI and machine learning for network automation, now handling 40% of fault management. We're developing 5G Advanced products and edge services. R&D focuses on RIC for energy savings and HyperStream for sub-2-second streaming latency.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one one. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding private 5G network deployments and SD-WAN integrations?

David Kim: Thanks, John. We're aggressively expanding in enterprise with private 5G and SD-WAN, as evidenced by our $500 million logistics deal covering 50+ warehouses for IoT and robotics. Our edge in midband spectrum and MEC positions us strongly against Verizon and AT&T. We've added 15,000 enterprise lines this quarter, with ACV up 11% to $45,000 via NaaS upsells. We'll continue leveraging Vodafone synergies in Europe and targeting Industry 4.0 in Japan, aiming for 10% total revenue by FY2027.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding capex and debt refinancing?

Michael Chen: Great question, Emily. Inflation at 3.8% and rates are manageable given our opex savings of $285 million and leverage at net 2.8x. We've locked sub-5% yields on $3.5 billion refinancings, cost down to 4.1%. Capex peaks at 14% this year tapering to 12%, offset by $6.2 billion FCF. AI efficiencies and Open RAN cut energy 22% and interconnect 18%, while tower monetizations delever 0.2x annually. We're resilient with $15 billion liquidity for any macro stress.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy efficiency in your 5G rollout?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Robert. Sustainability is core—we're targeting net-zero by 2040. Key initiatives include AI traffic management for 22% energy reduction per site, Open RAN for lower power, and fiber phasing out copper. We've divested sites for efficient lease-ups and use drone audits for FTTx. Success measured by KPIs like 250 bps annual margin gains tied to efficiencies, with 15% capex savings from mmWave trials. Progress tracked via monthly dashboards, aligning with EU Gigabit Act and BEAD.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth through our converged platform. Thank you for your time and interest in GlobalCom Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
